bug_semantics: An authenticated low-privilege CRM user can POST an attacker-controlled comment to the admin activities create route. ActivityController validates presence but passes request()->all() into ActivityRepository without neutralizing comment, ActivityResource returns the stored comment unchanged, and the shared activities component interprets it as HTML when another user views the activity. That stored-data-to-HTML-sink chain permits persistent attacker-controlled markup and, as reported by GHSA-j822-46r5-h4qx and upstream issue #2419, stored XSS across users including administrators.
flaw_origin: Commit fabc2c41978bad04d16b0a9098dd6288e68e3a06 made the first unsafe output-boundary transition in packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Resources/views/components/activities/index.blade.php: it replaced Vue's escaped @{{ activity.comment }} interpolation with v-html="activity.comment" while the create/update and JSON-resource paths continued carrying the comment verbatim. Commit 4848b68af8ce1b973fc60018860c8a8347d2b7bd later changed v-html to a DOMPurify-backed v-safe-html directive, reducing some script vectors but retaining HTML interpretation; the definitive fix restored escaped text interpolation.

Original analysis preserved: The vulnerability-first trace is complete: user-controlled comment enters through POST /admin/activities/create, is stored from request()->all(), is returned unchanged by ActivityResource, and crosses into an HTML-interpreting Vue sink. Line history proves fabc2c41978bad04d16b0a9098dd6288e68e3a06 is smaller and earlier than the later DOMPurify refactor: before fabc2c4 the direct parent used escaped Vue interpolation, while fabc2c4 first selected v-html. The later 4848b68 sanitizer change mitigated the raw sink but preserved markup interpretation and therefore did not restore the safe text boundary demonstrated by the final fix. The advisory-linked fc46704/v2.1.6 boundary is not causal for this activity-comment flaw; identical vulnerable source at v2.1.5, v2.1.6, and v2.2.3 plus upstream issue #2419's v2.1.6 reproduction proves that. PR #2542's one-line direct fix df1f2f, landed by f96e2f7 and first released in v2.2.4, restores escaped output. Because the exact BIC commit object is human-authored and has no AI attribution marker, the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
